logline: A legendary Las Vegas stand-up and a broke millennial comedy writer form an uneasy partnership that forces both women to confront what they have sacrificed for their careers.

bollymeter.basis: Perfect 100% Tomatometer from 75 critics at launch; Jean Smart's performance was called a career peak by multiple outlets, and the show won the Peabody Award and Emmy for Outstanding Comedy Series.

pull_quotes.text: Send this show to anyone who tells you women aren't funny - then enjoy this year's most perfect piece of television.
An industry satire as hilarious as it is scathing, Hacks is an odd-couple comedy perfectly suited for our modern age.

seasons.review_body: Hacks debuted May 13, 2021 on HBO Max to a perfect 100% Tomatometer from 75 critics. Jean Smart's performance as Deborah Vance, a Las Vegas comic whose audience is aging out of her material, was immediately cited as a career-defining turn. CNET called it the year's most perfect piece of television; them. praised its scathing industry satire. Hannah Einbinder's Ava - a young comedy writer blacklisted in Hollywood and desperate enough to take the Vegas gig - provided the generational friction the show needed. The odd-couple dynamic landed with critics as both emotionally precise and consistently funny. The show won the Peabody Award in 2022 and took the Emmy for Outstanding Comedy Series in its third season.

episode_reviews.title: There Is No Line
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The pilot establishes Deborah Vance as a woman at the peak of a diminishing empire - sold-out Vegas residency, declining cultural relevance - and Ava as someone with talent she cannot manage and a self-destruction she cannot explain. The episode does not condescend to either character.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Deborah's backstage routine - the efficiency and precision of a performer who has been doing this for decades, captured without sentimentality.

critic_note.text: The pacing is exquisite, with every episode revealing just enough backstory to cast them repeatedly in a new light.

episode_reviews.title: I Think She Will
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The season finale forces a reckoning between Deborah and Ava that makes explicit what the power dynamic between them has always meant. The show does not soften what the relationship costs, and the performances handle the ambiguity with full craft.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The road confrontation - the scene critics most cited as proof the show earned its emotional weight rather than manufactured it.

bollymeter.basis: 100% Tomatometer from 54 critics; the Guardian called it vicious and emotionally substantial, and the Atlantic praised the season for resisting the expected reconciliation arc.

pull_quotes.text: If good comedy needs emotional heft, this has it to spare, and still manages to be vicious.

seasons.review_body: Season 2 arrived May 12, 2022 and sustained the perfect 100% mark with 54 critics. The Guardian's Rebecca Nicholson called it vicious and emotionally substantial; the Atlantic argued the season worked precisely because it refused easy epiphanies and intergenerational bonding. The Times UK praised funnier jokes and more developed characters. The season took Deborah and Ava on the road, a structural choice that stripped away their Vegas comfort zones and pushed their dynamic into genuine friction. Jean Smart received her second consecutive Emmy nomination for Lead Actress, and the season confirmed the show was not a one-season anomaly.
seasons.season_over_season: Matches the first season's 100% with a road-trip structure that deepens the central relationship without softening its tensions; the Atlantic called the lack of easy bonding the season's key strength.

bollymeter.basis: 98% Tomatometer; RT consensus called it a persuasive argument for the show's own longevity; the season won the Emmy for Outstanding Comedy Series.

seasons.review_body: Season 3 premiered May 2, 2024 on Max and held 98% on Rotten Tomatoes. The RT consensus called it a reunion that never felt so good and a persuasive argument for the show's own longevity. The season won the Primetime Emmy for Outstanding Comedy Series, Jean Smart's fourth consecutive Lead Actress win confirmed her dominance of the category, and the Golden Globe for Best Musical or Comedy Series followed in 2025. Critics noted the new setting's productive disruption of the Deborah-Ava dynamic, and several reviewers argued Season 3 represented the show at its most formally ambitious.
seasons.season_over_season: Third season wins the Outstanding Comedy Series Emmy and confirms the show as the dominant comedy of its era; 98% critical approval down fractionally from two perfect scores but structurally stronger.

bollymeter.basis: 98% Tomatometer; continued acclaim for Jean Smart and Hannah Einbinder, with the show deepening its exploration of the industry cost of female ambition.

seasons.review_body: Season 4 premiered April 10, 2025 and maintained 98% on Rotten Tomatoes. Hannah Einbinder's Emmy win for Supporting Actress in 2025 confirmed the show's awards dominance across both its leads. Critics praised the season's willingness to complicate Ava's own ambition and complicity, shifting the show's moral geometry. The Golden Globe for Best Comedy Series in 2025 marked the show's second win in the category. At four seasons in, Hacks had established itself as one of the most consistently acclaimed comedies in prestige television history.
seasons.season_over_season: Sustains 98% critical approval while deepening Ava's agency and moral complexity; Einbinder's Emmy win shifted the show's awards profile from a one-woman performance showcase to a genuine ensemble.

bollymeter.basis: 97% Tomatometer for the series finale season; critics called it a worthy conclusion to one of the prestige era's most consistently celebrated comedies.

seasons.review_body: The fifth and final season concluded May 28, 2026 on Max with 97% on Rotten Tomatoes. Critics praised the finale season for resolving the Deborah-Ava relationship without flattening the tensions that gave the show its energy. The overall 98% aggregate across 253 reviews represents one of the highest multi-season critical averages in prestige comedy history. The show's five-season run - from HBO Max launch to Max finale - mapped the streaming comedy's maturation over half a decade, and Hacks remained its benchmark.
seasons.season_over_season: Series conclusion at 97% maintains the standard set across four seasons; critics called the finale both earned and appropriately unresolved.
